newsitem.title: CANADA: Laidlaw to acquire American Medical for US$1.12 bln.
newsitem.headline: Laidlaw to acquire American Medical for US$1.12 bln.

text.p: Canadian waste and transportation giant Laidlaw Inc. said on Monday that it plans to acquire Colorado-based American Medical Response Inc. in a US$1.12 billion cash deal and merge it with its California-based MedTrans ambulance services unit.

Laidlaw, based in Burlington, Ontario, also said it has signed a letter of intent to sell its South Carolina-based Environmental Services unit for cash, shares and debt to Rollins Environmental Services Inc. of Delaware.
Laidlaw said in a statement that it will offer US$40 a share for each of American Medical's 28 million common shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis.

American Medical's board has received a fairness opinion from its financial advisor, Smith Barney Inc., and recommends that shareholders accept the offer, Laidlaw said. It plans to make a tender offer within five business days.

The deal is expected to close in February. The transaction will immediately add to Laidlaw's earnings and the merged company will continue to operate as American Medical Response Inc., the company said.
In another transaction, Laidlaw said it plans to sell its Environmental Services unit to Rollins Environmental Services for US$400 million in cash, plus Rollins stock and a convertible bond.
